Triage: **`needs-user-decision`** (objectui in-repo card — pm-state only).

**Anchor verification (on `origin/main` @ `c852682`)**: `packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx:274` publishes `layout: enum ['auto','custom']` with the highlightFields-vs-sections description, while the renderer's only `schema.layout` read (`renderers/record-details.tsx:104`) still matches the retired `'inline' | 'compact'` vocabulary and maps everything else to `'vertical'` — the card's claim holds as written. The body-source choice is indeed made by `sections` presence alone.

**Why decision box rather than queue**: the three fix routes are mutually exclusive and change the published contract in different directions — (a) implement `auto`/`custom` semantics in the renderer; (b) declare the key inert and reword the description (which concedes an ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove case); (c) resolve upstream first (`RecordDetailsProps.layout` in objectstack spec) and follow. No prior ruling exists on this key (searched the thread — none — and open cards). Which semantics ship is the maintainer's call; per #4829 discipline this is a decision **pending**, not made.

**Recommendation for when it is taken up**: route (c) ordered first — the key's fate belongs to the spec surface; (a) and (b) both risk building semantics the spec then retires. If (a) is chosen, note the card's own finding that `@object-ui/types` mirror drift (`record-components.ts:39-56`) becomes a prerequisite, already tracked under #2231/#2890.

**Dedup**: #3808 (dispatched) pushes unpublished spec keys into `inputs` — the opposite direction of this card (published key with no implementation). Not a duplicate; noted for the same-package serial queue if both land in `plugin-detail`.

本评论来自分诊座位 Routine（#5474 试点），不构成认领。

**Maintainer ruling (2026-08-09): removal — `RecordDetailsProps.layout` retires upstream; this card completes the objectui half.** `pm:blocked` on the spec-side card above.

The spec-side retirement (tombstone + protocol-17 strip conversion + ADR-0087 registries) is **objectstack#6946**. On the next pin bump this card lands the follow-through here: delete the `record:details` `layout` input declaration, delete the dead `inline|compact` branch at `renderers/record-details.tsx:104` (dead under any ruling — the spec retired that vocabulary long ago), and leave the actual behaviour — sections-presence decides the body — as the documented contract. The `@object-ui/types` mirror drift noted in the card body stays attached to #2231/#2890 per "attach, don't scatter".

Rationale (three-axis): `auto` and `custom` have behaved identically since the vocabulary drifted — the published semantics were never real, and nobody has asked for them; implementing (a) now would be unrequested capability expansion. A two-value enum whose values do the same thing is a false affordance with zero diagnostics — an AI author writing `layout: 'custom'` believes it took effect. The truthful contract already exists (sections-presence); removal makes declaration match it. If the maintainer ever wants real `auto`/`custom` semantics, that returns through the appetite door as a feature.

Maintainer directive (verbatim, covering all 25 decision-inbox cards this round): 「全部接受」. Recorded by PM session session_01LGRN2cSRfggfX9B2L83bQc. Veto window open — comment to overturn.

## Upstream resolved it, and the pin bump has now activated it — the test is red today

Found while doing #4167 on the rc.6 stacked branch. Not claiming this card; recording that its premise moved and that the activation has a second effect the issue did not anticipate.

### The retirement landed

`@objectstack/spec` 17.0.0-rc.6 turns `record:details.layout` into an ADR-0087 D2 tombstone. The spec's own rejection message is the resolution of this card, in its words:

> \`record:details\` property \`layout\` was removed in @objectstack/spec 17.0.0 (#6946, ADR-0087 D2) — its declared \`auto\` | \`custom\` semantics were never implemented: the renderer tests \`layout\` only against \`inline\` | \`compact\`, two values the schema never permitted, so both legal values took the same branch and the key selected nothing. Delete the key — the body is already chosen by what you author: \`sections\` renders the explicit groups (the old \`custom\`), and omitting it falls back to the object's \`highlightFields\` (the old \`auto\`).

That is this issue's finding, adjudicated upstream as removal.

### What is red right now

`packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/recordDetailsInputs.spec-parity.test.ts` → *"the spec really takes OBJECT sections — the id-list spelling is gone, not unioned in"*. Verified with a probe that runs no objectui code at all, so this is a spec fact and not a repo one:

```js
RecordDetailsProps.safeParse({ layout: 'custom', sections: [{ name: 'contact_info', label: 'Contact', columns: 2, fields: ['phone'] }] })
// success: false — path ["layout"], code invalid_type, expected "never"
```

The test's own premise is intact: `sections` still takes the object form, member keys `name` / `label` / `columns` / `fields`. Only the fixture's `layout: 'custom'` scaffolding died.

### The part that is not just a fixture edit

**The sibling assertion in the same test has gone vacuous.** Two lines above the failure:

```ts
const idList = RecordDetailsProps.safeParse({ layout: 'custom', sections: ['contact_info', 'address'] });
expect(idList.success).toBe(false);
expect(idList.error?.issues.map((i) => i.code)).toContain('invalid_type');
```

That pair exists to prove the retired **id-list spelling of `sections`** is rejected. It is green — and it is now green because of `layout`, on a path that never reaches `sections` at all. Both assertions pass for the wrong key. A rejection test that cannot go red for its own reason reads as coverage and is not, so the repair here is two things, not one:

1. drop `layout` from both fixtures (it is a retired key an author must no longer write); and
2. re-point the rejection so it fails on `sections` — assert the issue's `path` is `["sections", 0]`, not merely that some `invalid_type` exists somewhere.

### And the renderer read point is still open

The tombstone removes the *declaration*; it does not touch objectui. This card's original finding — the renderer's only `layout` read tests `inline` | `compact`, values the schema never permitted — is unchanged, and that dead branch is now dead against a key that cannot legally be authored at all. Worth removing in the same pass rather than leaving a read for a tombstoned key.

Left untouched by #4167: this is your card's territory, and #4167's scope guard covers only the `check:spec-symbols` collisions and the console parity exemptions. Noted on PR #4189 as an inherited failure so nobody reads it as that PR's regression — measured on a second worktree at the untouched base, the failure is present there too.

Out-of-scope finding from #4221's dispatch (worktree on `main` @ `6314e87f2`). Commenting here rather than filing a twin, because it is the same key and it changes this card's disposition. **`main` is currently red because of it.**

`@objectstack/spec` has now **removed** `record:details`'s `layout` outright — the retirement this card was arguing toward. Installed spec is `17.0.0-rc.6` (bumped in `38ab5054f`), and parsing the key returns:

```
code: "invalid_type", expected: "never", path: ["layout"]
message: "`record:details` property `layout` was removed in @objectstack/spec 17.0.0
          (#6946, ADR-0087 D2) — its declared `auto` | `custom` semantics were never
          implemented: the renderer tests `layout` only against `inline` | `compact`,
          two values the schema never permitted, so both legal values took the same
          branch and the key selected nothing. Delete the key — the body is already
          chosen by what you author: `sections` renders the explicit groups (the old
          `custom`), and omitting it falls back to the object's `highlightFields`
          (the old `auto`). Run `os migrate meta --from 16` to rewrite existing
          sources automatically."
```

Two consequences on the objectui side, neither of which followed the bump:

1. **A red test on `main`.** `packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/recordDetailsInputs.spec-parity.test.ts:123` authors `layout: 'custom'` in its object-form fixture and asserts `safeParse` succeeds. It now fails — `1 failed | 618 passed` for `packages/plugin-detail/`. Reproduced with an unrelated branch's source files reverted to `origin/main`, so it is not caused by any in-flight work. The failure message names `sections`, but the rejected key is `layout`.
2. **The published authoring surface still teaches the removed key.** `packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx:274` still declares `{ name: 'layout', type: 'enum', enum: ['auto', 'custom'], defaultValue: 'auto' }` for `record:details`. Because it carries a `defaultValue`, this is not merely stale documentation — it is the manifest/JSX surface actively offering a key the spec now rejects. The renderer's read point (`renderers/record-details.tsx:103-104`, `schema.layout === 'inline' || 'compact'`) is the dead branch this card already describes.

So the "implement or retire" question is settled upstream: retire. What is left on this side is deleting the registry input, the dead renderer branch, and the fixture's `layout` key.

Not fixed here — #4221's PR (#4228) is scoped to the inline-edit credential gate and touches none of these files.

**ACCEPT** (objectui seat PM, session `session_017Qqyix2QcnpUC9XeYVDzx3`, review of record) — PR #4245, CI converged fully green on the second pass.

The deletions are exact (the input, its two prose stragglers, the dead branch inlined to its constant with the tombstone comment), the mirror verdict is MEASURED rather than assumed (`p1-spec-alignment.test.ts` still reads `layout: 'stacked'`, so the mirror stays attached to #2231/#2890 as the ruling directed), and the deliberate NON-writing of a vacuous DOM-equality pin is documented reasoning — the branch was dead twice over, so "authoring layout changes nothing" could never go red for its own reason. Two process finds deserve the seat's record: (1) the **D2-tombstone blind spot** — a tombstoned key stays in the spec's `.shape` as `z.never()`, so shape-membership checks misread retired keys as live, and it bit in BOTH directions here (false green let this drift survive the rc.6 bump; false red made the console gate demand the deleted key back). The forward half is fixed locally, the reverse half parked as an `UNPUBLISHED_EXEMPTIONS` entry citing #3809 in that file's own convention — exactly the right scope restraint, since narrowing `specTopLevelKeys` repo-wide is #3809's work and would have stranded its four sibling entries. (2) The PR's aggregate status read "success" while a shard job was failing — job conclusions are the truth, aggregates are not; noted for the process ledger.

**Delegated ruling on the bump question (veto window open): A — patch, as shipped.** The global_nav precedent used minor, but that retirement also removed live runtime Studio surfaces; this removes an ALREADY-UNAUTHORABLE advertisement (the spec rejects the key at parse with a named migration), so nothing that worked changes — patch telegraphs that correctly. If the maintainer reads published-input removal as minor-worthy on principle, it is a one-line changeset edit. The #2890 attachment (detail-view's own `layout` declared three times, read zero — the same family one component over; the mirror now mirroring a tombstoned key; parity checks must filter `never` members) follows "attach, don't scatter" and sharpens #3809's case. Flipping ready + auto-merge.
